This is reminiscent of problem "Maximum Number of Groups With Increasing Length" from LeetCode (weekly contest?). The solution: Sort usageLimits in non-decreasing order. Then greedily build groups: keep a running sum of usageLimits; each time sum >= required total elements for groups so far (i.e., sum_{j=1}^{k} j = k(k+1)/2), we can form k groups.

Reason: For groups with sizes 1,2,3,...,k, total number of elements needed (counting repetitions across groups) is sum_{i=1}^k i = k(k+1)/2. Since each group must have distinct numbers (no repeats within group) but numbers can be reused across groups up to usageLimits[i] times, the feasibility condition reduces to: we need enough total "capacity" (sum of usageLimits) to cover the total required slots across groups. Additionally, we need to be able to assign distinct numbers within each group; but if we sort usageLimits and allocate smallest capacities to fill early groups, we can always satisfy distinctness condition as long as total capacity >= required slots.
